shared.subjectLabel: FINAL WORDING SUBJECT TO PILOT AGREEMENT

hero.title: Test PYXIS-1 on the music that [[matters to your team.]]
hero.sub: A managed private pilot for labels, distributors and catalogue teams. Test sonic discovery on authorised material, with success criteria agreed up front.
hero.trustline: MANAGED EVALUATION · PARTNER-SCOPED · NO PUBLIC SANDBOX
hero.protocolLabel: The pilot protocol · One sample, six stages
hero.protocolAria: The pilot protocol: one representative catalogue sample moves through six stages on a single line: scope, ingest, index, test, measure and decide. Each stage is a station on the protocol rail; the decision stage is highlighted as the destination.
hero.protocolNote: agree the questions and success criteria before reviewing the results
hero.protocolNoteDim: one bounded process · evidence at every stage

mobileStages.title: Scope
mobileStages.body: Agree the question, the sample and the success criteria.

mobileStages.title: Ingest
mobileStages.body: Deliver audio + CSV manifest through managed SFTP.

mobileStages.title: Index
mobileStages.body: Validation, PYXIS-1 processing, private index build.

mobileStages.title: Test
mobileStages.body: Ranked results from your agreed reference set.

mobileStages.title: Measure
mobileStages.body: Expert review against the agreed scorecard.

mobileStages.title: Decide
mobileStages.body: Joint findings review: stop, extend or plan production.

qualification.title: Built for catalogue teams with a real question to test

matrix.question: Can older tracks be surfaced from current references?
Are our catalogue relationships discoverable beyond metadata?
Where does our current catalogue search break down?
Can similarity fit inside our current product and journey?
Does the analysis produce useful structured data for briefs?

qualification.interpBold: You must control or be authorised to supply the evaluation material.
qualification.interpBody: Submitting an inquiry starts a conversation about fit; not every request becomes a pilot right away.
strongFit: Willing to agree measures up front
needsScoping: Very small or highly uniform sample

pilotPack.title: Bring a representative sample, not the full catalogue
pilotPack.lead: We scope sample size and mix together, around your use case and the range of the catalogue.

items.title: Authorised audio
items.body: MP3, WAV, FLAC or AIFF: material you control or are authorised to supply.

items.title: CSV metadata
items.body: One row per track: ISRC, title, artist and filename, all required. BPM, duration and release details are optional.

items.title: Current + older repertoire
items.body: A meaningful mix, with enough related recordings to test similarity properly.

items.title: Known reference tracks
items.body: Tracks your team already knows: the anchors the evaluation is scored against.

items.title: Expert reviewers
items.body: A small group of catalogue experts or selectors who will judge relevance.

items.title: A clear use case
items.body: The question the pilot should answer: discovery, catalogue or product.

items.title: Optional event data
items.body: Only where you want to evaluate product behaviour downstream.

pilotPack.footnote: no universal track count; the sample is scoped around the use case, not a number

method.title: One bounded process. Six clear stages.
method.lead: Every stage states what Resomix does, what your team does, and what evidence it produces.

scorecard.title: Agree the scorecard before you see the results
scorecard.lead: No pre-filled percentages and no fabricated outcomes: targets are agreed in scoping, results are measured in the pilot.
scorecard.tableAria: Pilot scorecard: each measure with how it is assessed; target and result fields are intentionally empty until agreed and measured
scorecard.latencyNote: search on indexed tracks and processing of uploads are timed separately, never merged into one "search speed" figure
scorecard.optBtnClosed: Optional product measures, where you supply event data ▸
scorecard.optBtnOpen: Optional product measures, where you supply event data ▾
scorecard.optTableAria: Optional product measures, used only where the partner supplies event data

deliverables.title: A decision pack, not a sales demo
deliverables.body: The pilot ends with evidence your team can act on: what worked, what didn't, where the limits are, and what production would involve. Final deliverables are agreed during scoping.

outcomes.title: Stop
outcomes.body: The evidence does not justify expansion. A clean, documented end.

outcomes.title: Extend
outcomes.body: A second bounded test, on another catalogue area or question.

outcomes.title: Plan production
outcomes.body: Scope, ingestion cadence, API usage, service mode and terms, agreed together.

deliverables.footnote: the pilot does not automatically convert into a contract · no public prices on this page
deliverables.reportTruth: TYPICAL OUTPUTS · FINAL SCOPE AGREED BEFORE INGEST
deliverables.reportAria: A sample pilot findings dossier: a report-styled panel listing the typical outputs: scope and criteria, ingestion validation summary, indexed sample, evaluation access, relevance scorecard, performance summary, catalogue observations, technical findings, limitations and open questions, production options, joint review session.

handling.title: Your sample stays inside the agreed pilot boundary

trustItems.text: Partner catalogues are logically isolated and restricted to authorised partner access.
You keep ownership and commercial control of your catalogue throughout.
Partner content is not used to train or fine-tune PYXIS-1. It is not a model, and it does not generate derivative audio.
Public exposure is not part of the pilot.
Your sample is processed within a partner-scoped catalogue boundary and restricted to authorised access. Detailed access, retention and deletion terms are agreed before ingestion.

form.title: Tell us what you want to explore
form.lead: Tell us about your catalogue, API integration or potential pilot. Submitting this form doesn't create an account or automatically start a pilot.
